languages.name: Even number of 0s
languages.description: Binary strings containing an even number of 0s (the empty string has zero 0s).
languages.ml_note: Parity is a counting property; generic count-mod-k features make it learnable.

languages.name: Ends with "01"
languages.description: Binary strings whose last two symbols are "01".
languages.ml_note: A local suffix pattern; last-k / suffix features capture it directly.

languages.name: Contains "101"
languages.description: Binary strings containing the substring "101" somewhere.
languages.ml_note: Substring presence equals a non-zero 3-gram count, which is a generic feature.

languages.name: Number of 1s divisible by 3
languages.description: Binary strings whose count of 1s is a multiple of 3 (zero counts).
languages.ml_note: Modular counting: learnable only because count-mod-3 is among the generic features.

languages.name: No two consecutive 1s
languages.description: Binary strings that never contain "11" (Fibonacci-many strings per length).
languages.ml_note: Forbidden factor: the 2-gram count of 11 must be zero.

languages.name: Binary multiple of 3
languages.description: Binary numbers (MSB first) whose value is divisible by 3. Leading zeros are allowed and the empty string denotes 0.
languages.ml_note: Needs position-weighted sums mod 3; no generic feature encodes it, so ML is expected to struggle.

languages.name: (a|b)*abb
languages.description: Strings over {a,b} ending in "abb" - the classic NFA example from the Dragon Book.
languages.ml_note: Suffix pattern; easy for suffix / last-k features.

languages.name: Length ≡ 0 (mod 4) and starts with a
languages.description: Strings over {a,b} that start with 'a' and whose length is a multiple of 4 (so the empty string is rejected).
languages.ml_note: Length mod 4 is a generic feature, and the first symbol is a positional feature.

languages.name: Third symbol from the end is 1
languages.description: Binary strings of length >= 3 whose third-to-last symbol is 1. Its 4-state NFA needs 2^3 = 8 DFA states (exponential blow-up).
languages.ml_note: Positional features for the last 6 symbols expose it directly.

languages.name: #a − #b ≡ 0 (mod 3)
languages.description: Strings over {a,b} where the number of a's minus the number of b's is a multiple of 3.
languages.ml_note: Needs an interaction of two residues (#a mod 3, #b mod 3): no linear model over the one-hot residues can separate it.

insights: The ground-truth automata are exact by construction (proved with the product construction) and use 2-8 states.

Passive learning from the labelled training strings: EDSM recovered the exact minimal DFA for 10/10 languages, RPNI for 8/10 (misses: L2 (shortest wrong string '1'), L7 (shortest wrong string 'bb'), where the split moved a few of the shortest strings out of training).

L* extracted a DFA equivalent to the ground truth from 34 of 40 pipelines: 31 converged (the model implements the language exactly) and 3 stopped at the state budget (the DFA reflects the model's short-string behaviour; see fidelity).
Mean test accuracy of the ML pipelines: Logistic Regression 0.921, Decision Tree 0.972, Random Forest 0.976, Stacked ensemble 0.975; on unseen lengths 21-40: 0.906, 0.911, 0.934, 0.915.

L6 (binary multiples of 3) defeats every ML pipeline (about 0.53 on long strings): no generic feature encodes a position-weighted sum mod 3. L10 defeats the linear model, and on long strings also the trees.
A DFA classifies a string in about 0.5 microseconds with a handful of states; the random forests carry about 17,769 tree nodes on average.
Converged extractions that still differ from the truth pinpoint the model's error exactly: L8/Logistic Regression on '' ('' = the empty string).
